steps.what: Write the original literary draft in the author's own voice
inputs: author's ideas and chosen literary form

steps.what: Read and revise the literary pieces for voice, structure and effect
Apply the intended manuscript formatting to the literary pieces
Save the original literary manuscript in the existing authoring file

tasks.design: Use native manuscript styles in {DOCS} for repeated layout while the teacher writes and revises the original literary text. The change affects formatting only; authorship and literary decisions stay with the writer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layout adjustments surround creative writing and revision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native paragraph and manuscript styles remove repeated formatting without generating the literary work.
tasks.still_hard: An original literary voice and deliberate effect are the purpose of the work.
tasks.human_edge: Choose language, perspective and form for an intended artistic effect.

ambition.what: The teacher remains the literary author.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document styles reduce repeated manuscript formatting while original writing and literary revision remain authorial work.

assumptions: Boundary is writing and preparing the actual manuscript, not journal submission, publication or a new creative-work log.
The author supplies the ideas, text and layout choices in the counted writing and formatting steps. No external brief, clean transcript or model-written substitute is assumed.

s3 removes2.1 units of repeated paragraph layout, retaining11.9 for form-specific formatting and checking. All85 writing and revision units remain. Native styles already used earn no additional benefit.
The one-unit ordinary author save is fully retained and ungated. No self-approval or publication commitment is added to saving a draft.
unknowns: Actual formatting burden and use of styles
research_questions: Does the literary form permit reusable styles without altering intentional spacing?

already_counted.description: Write, revise, finish formatting and save the original manuscript

incremental.description: Maintain manuscript styles and repair unintended spacing changes

steps.what: Read student organizations' actual proposals and relevant institutional publication guidance
Act as advisers in discussion with student organizations about their own plans

tasks.design: Keep current institutional publication guidance directly linked beside the actual student proposal in {DOCS}. The teacher reads the material and advises the student group in person or by call, leaving its literary and organizational choices with the students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation sometimes involves finding the appropriate guidance for a student publication or literary event.
tasks.enabler_now: A native source link removes a little navigation without replacing adviser reading.
tasks.still_hard: Students need space to make their own editorial and organizational choices.
tasks.human_edge: Encourage a student's judgement while raising practical concerns respectfully.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: direct access to existing publication guidance can slightly reduce adviser preparation while student-group discussion remains human.

assumptions: OTHER means the ordinary adviser meeting. The scenario is a student literary organization, including actual proposal reading, not a new adviser report or a formal publication approval.
Students produce the proposal and institutional staff maintain the guidance. s1 counts the teacher's reading; no new student questionnaire, minutes or summary is assumed.

s1 removes one unit of guidance navigation, retaining24 for reading the proposal and relevant rules. All75 discussion units remain. Existing direct links earn no new benefit and no record write is hidden in the conversation.
research_questions: Is there repeated source navigation beyond reading the student proposal?

steps.what: Define the research project and funding proposal's actual methods and resource needs
Read the external funding call and identify proposal requirements
Calculate the research funding budget from specified quantities and authorised rates
Draft the grant proposal narrative from the actual research design and sources

loop.purpose: Express the researcher's specified project in the required proposal structure
loop.input: research design, verified sources, call requirements and calculated budget
loop.output: complete narrative with source references and explicit resource commitments
loop.check: Teacher checks the intellectual argument, feasibility, citations and every claimed commitment against the actual project in s5
loop.stop: Two drafts maximum; invented references or unsupported commitments return to funded manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Native forms give structure but cannot assemble the project-specific scholarly argument from the researcher's material

steps.what: Read and correct the complete research grant proposal and budget
Check the final grant proposal and authorise the institution's exact funding application
Submit the exact authorised research funding proposal to the funder

tasks.design: Generate the specified budget in {SPREADSHEET} and draft the researcher's proposal in {DOCS} from the actual call, design and verified references. The teacher corrects the scholarly argument and commitments, then the existing research office authorises the complete application before submission through the funder's portal {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget arithmetic and narrative assembly repeat after the researcher has designed the project.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic budget rules and a bounded evidence-linked drafting loop reduce assembly without choosing the research.
tasks.still_hard: A fundable argument needs original scholarship, feasible methods and honest resource commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Develop and defend the project's intellectual contribution.

ambition.what: The teacher remains the research designer and proposal owner.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed budget calculations and project-specific proposal drafts can reduce grant assembly while research design and institutional submission authority remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means the actual funder application portal. Boundary includes an institutional grant proposal, existing research-office authorisation and real submission, not grant review or an assumed increase in award probability.

s1 counts the teacher's design, source selection and specification of resource items, quantities and timings. The funder produces call requirements; finance maintains authorised rates. Missing fields and nonstandard budget categories require funded manual repair.

s3 replaces actual manual arithmetic. s4 drafts only from the researcher's own design and verified publications; no confidential third-party proposal is uploaded. Native forms and templates are tried before the narrative loop; existing runtime earns no saving.

s5 retains all15 units of scholarly and factual correction. s6 is the institution's actual independent submission-authority check after the final version exists, not author approval of an internal save. Any changed narrative, budget or attachment invalidates the submission snapshot.
The actual one-unit submission and ordinary ungated document save remain fully retained. Approved processing arrangements must exist for the proposal material.
research_questions: Can every citation and resource commitment be traced to the researcher's actual project and the current call?

already_counted.description: Design the research, read the call, correct the complete application and submit
Research office checks the final institutional application

incremental.description: Maintain budget mappings and manually repair missing categories, unsupported citations or failed prose drafts

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected proposal, budget, attachments and funder destination authorised in s6; changes require renewed institutional authority

steps.what: Read the manuscript for its professional contribution, argument and evidence
Enter the manuscript's public bibliographic identifiers needing reference checks
Resolve the manuscript's bibliographic identifiers against authoritative catalogue records
outputs: resolved reference records and unresolved flags

steps.what: Write the professional manuscript review with reasons and publication recommendation
inputs: resolved reference records and unresolved flags

steps.what: Read the complete manuscript review for accuracy, confidentiality and recommendation consistency
outputs: checked reviewer report and editor destination

steps.what: Submit only the checked manuscript review to the journal editor
inputs: checked reviewer report and editor destination

tasks.design: Use an allowed native bibliographic resolver {OTHER} for public reference identifiers while keeping the manuscript and review in the journal's authorised environment and {DOCS}. The teacher performs the substantive reading and writes and checks the review before its exact submission; no model receives or judges the manuscript.
tasks.previous_blocker: Public citation identifiers are repeatedly looked up during a confidential review.
tasks.enabler_now: Exact identifier resolution removes fixed lookup while preserving full scholarly judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Reference existence does not establish that a manuscript's interpretation or contribution is sound.
tasks.human_edge: Evaluate the argument fairly and explain the recommendation with precise reasons.

ambition.what: Scholarly peer review remains the teacher's work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: exact public bibliographic identifiers can be resolved deterministically, while confidential manuscript assessment and review writing remain human scholarly work.

assumptions: OTHER means an authorised bibliographic catalogue and the journal's reviewer portal. Boundary is the real peer-review report and submission, not editorial publication approval or grant evaluation.

The journal supplies the manuscript and criteria. s1 counts substantive reading and reference selection; s2 counts manual identifier capture and checking. The catalogue supplies public reference records, not a verdict on the manuscript.

s3 replaces actual manual identifier lookup only. Unresolved records require funded manual catalogue checks and all interpretation remains in s1 and s4. Native resolver use already present earns no new saving.

Journal confidentiality and tool rules must permit the actual public-identifier lookup; no full manuscript or review is uploaded to a model. If metadata cannot leave the journal environment, the resolver must operate there or the work stays manual.

s5 is the reviewer's ordinary final accuracy and confidentiality check of the real outgoing report, not a new approval of an internal save. It binds the exact report and editor destination for s6, and edits require another check. The current one-unit submission and ordinary ungated save earn no saving.
unknowns: Journal's actual confidentiality and tool permissions
research_questions: Can public identifiers be resolved without transmitting confidential manuscript content?

already_counted.description: Assess the manuscript, capture reference identifiers, write and check the actual review and submit

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue access and manually resolve failed or ambiguous identifiers

approvals.approved_version: Exact reviewer report, confidentiality scope and editor destination checked in s5; edits void submission readiness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90 gross10 less upkeep2 gives8. For archival references with few resolvable identifiers, catalogue lookup retains8 of10 and all90 other units remain. Gross2 is offset by upkeep2, giving low0. No manuscript judgement, review writing or tiny send runtime is counted as saved.
